extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of computer algebra systems, especially researchers in commutative algebra, algebraic geometry, and singularity theory
extracted.subtask_description: An overview of the SINGULAR computer algebra system highlighting the functional criteria and features by which the system can be judged (targeted at polynomial computations in commutative algebra/algebraic geometry/singularity theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on target mathematical fields
rubrics_metrics.description: SINGULAR is a Computer Algebra System for polynomial computations with special emphasis on the needs of commutative algebra, algebraic geometry, and singularity theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the system is designed and optimized for workflows and problems commonly arising in these three mathematical areas; suitability for these fields should be a primary evaluation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main computational objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Main computational objects: ideals/modules over very general polynomial rings over various ground fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system must support ideals and modules, work over general polynomial rings, and handle multiple ground fields—important when selecting a CAS for algebraic tasks involving these structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms implemented in kernel (performance/robustness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large variety of algorithms implemented in kernel (written in C/C++).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kernel-implemented algorithms (in C/C++) imply performance and reliability; evaluate the presence and variety of core algorithms and their native implementation for speed and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming language usability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system provides an imperative, C-like language for user programming—assess readability, ease of scripting, and learning curve, especially for users familiar with C-like syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensibility via libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Many more algorithms implemented as SINGULAR libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of modular libraries expands functionality; evaluate the breadth, quality, and ease of integrating libraries and writing new ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability with other CAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication links connect SINGULAR with other CAS's like MMA or MuPAD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to interoperate (data exchange, calling routines) with other computer algebra systems to leverage external tools and workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation availability and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive documentation: Manual, Tutorial (info, ps, and html).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive documentation in multiple formats is provided; evaluate completeness, clarity, tutorial availability, and ease of access for learning and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability, platform support, and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Freely available for most hard- and software platforms (Unix, Windows, Macintosh) from ftp://www.mathematik.uni-kl.de/pub/Math/Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the software is free, which platforms are supported, and how easy it is to obtain and install; licensing and distribution method affect adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maturity and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Development started in 1984; Current stable version: 2.0.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long development history and stable releases indicate maturity; evaluate release cadence, stability of the current version, and backward compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and applications provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples, Applications (sections listed on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of worked examples and described applications helps users assess applicability to real problems; evaluate quantity and relevance of examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community, contributors, and future roadmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors, History, Future (sections listed on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about contributors and planned future development indicates community support and sustainability; assess activity level, contributor base, and roadmap transparency.
